heroHeadline: Day 601: USMCA Bilateral Round Opens; CNTE Strike Begins; FGR Summons Two Governors; Sheinbaum Announces Global Millionaire Tax Plan
heroSubtitle: May 25, 2026 marks Day 601 of Claudia Sheinbaum's presidency. The first formal U.S.–Mexico USMCA bilateral review round opened today in Mexico City, covering rules of origin, Chinese nearshoring restrictions, energy market access, and steel tariffs ahead of the July 1 decision deadline — arriving three days after the historic EU-Mexico Modernised Global Agreement signing (May 22). Also today: the CNTE dissident teacher union launched a strike and march in Mexico City, with a mega-march and Zócalo encampment planned for June 1 during FIFA World Cup international visibility. At her mañanera, Sheinbaum confirmed Mexico will join 11 other heads of state in signing a global millionaire tax initiative in Barcelona; addressed FGR subpoenas of Sinaloa Governor Rocha Moya (DOJ narco-conspiracy probe) and Chihuahua Governor Maru Campos (CIA-Chihuahua witness), pledging no political persecution; and confirmed Sara Carter's (U.S. Drug Czar) visit postponed again. Day 600 (May 24, Sunday): Sheinbaum held a welfare rally in Teapa, Tabasco presenting the 'Segundo Piso del Bienestar' package — 24 billion pesos for 708,000 Tabasco beneficiaries, including home health visits, new hospitals, and pension delivery to women aged 60–64 — and announced a May 31 national accountability report broadcast to all 32 states' public plazas. Citi's May 21 survey lowered the 2026 full-year GDP growth forecast to 1.1%, the weakest consensus since 2020, citing USMCA uncertainty and tariff drag.
